subject: english-literature
title: Feminism and Psychoanalysis
welcome_lead: Two lenses that re-read the canon: feminist critique unmasks patriarchy; psychoanalysis maps the unconscious.
meta_desc: Feminist criticism and psychoanalytic criticism (Freud, Lacan) at A-Level English Literature.
final_note: You have read with feminism and the unconscious — two of the most generative twentieth-century critical lenses.

concepts.def: Reading literature for its construction and critique of gender (Woolf, Showalter, Gilbert & Gubar, Cixous).
Elaine Showalter's term — feminist criticism focused on women writers and their traditions.
Gilbert and Gubar (1979) — patriarchal literature's confinement of women between angel and monster.
Reading for unconscious desires, repression, the Oedipus complex and dream-work.
Reading through Jacques Lacan's mirror stage, the symbolic order and the Real.
Hélène Cixous's term — feminine writing that disrupts patriarchal language (The Laugh of the Medusa, 1975).

walkthroughs.body_html:
Virginia Woolf's A Room of One's Own (1929) asked what women writers needed — money and space. Showalter's gynocriticism mapped a female literary tradition.

Gilbert and Gubar diagnosed the angel/monster binary at the heart of patriarchal narrative.
Freudian criticism reads texts as dreams — manifest content hiding latent desire. The uncanny (das Unheimliche, 1919) names the disturbing familiarity of the repressed returning.

Lacan's mirror stage (1949) describes how the infant misrecognises itself in the mirror as whole. Entry into the symbolic order (language) is loss.

Lacanian readings track how characters are caught between desire and the Other.

mcqs.q: What is the function of dystopian fiction?
options: Dystopian fiction predicts what will actually happen in 100 years.
To critique tendencies in the writer's own society by extrapolating them into a nightmarish future — dystopias hold up a warning mirror to the present.
Dystopian fiction is just storytelling set in scary futures.
An unreliable narrator is when the author makes mistakes.
Their account is undermined within the text by ignorance, bias, self-deception or deceit, so the reader must read against what they say.
An unreliable narrator is when the author makes mistakes.
An unreliable narrator is one who tells lies in the story.
Dystopian fiction predicts what will actually happen in 100 years.

mcqs.q: Why are genre conventions important when interpreting a text?
options: Genre is just a label to help bookshops categorise novels.
Genre means whether a book is fiction or non-fiction.
They set reader expectations the text can fulfil or subvert; analysing how a text uses or breaks conventions reveals its meaning and significance.
Dystopian fiction predicts what will actually happen in 100 years.
